evals.name: tlv-property-purchase-encumbrances-and-env
evals.prompt: I'm about to sign on a 4-dunam plot off Yigal Alon in Tel Aviv next Tuesday. The seller's lawyer sent me a one-page letter that says the property is 'free and clear of all encumbrances' and that 'there are no environmental issues with the lot'. The price is ~₪12M and we're putting down a 20% deposit at signing. What should I actually check before I sign, and how do I verify those two claims? Include stuff that costs money if it's worth it.
evals.expected_output: Three-tier verification plan for the encumbrance and environmental claims: T1 sources named specifically (Tabu nesach, Registrar of Pledges, Ministry of Environmental Protection registries, planning portal); T2 critique of the seller's letter (incentive to misrepresent); T3 escalations named with cost bands (title insurance, Phase I ESA). A risk register with all 8 fields. A must-tell residuals list at the top. No 'go/no-go' opinion.

evals.name: vendor-dd-financials-and-iso27001
evals.prompt: We're about to sign a 3-year, ~$2M/year managed-services contract with a vendor based in Eastern Europe. They sent me a PDF of their audited financials (signed by a firm I haven't heard of) and a copy of their ISO 27001 certificate (issued by a body called 'EuroCert ITS'). My CFO wants me to make sure these documents are real and that the company is a going concern before we sign. How should I approach this?
evals.expected_output: Verification plan that treats both documents as T2 with a strong incentive to misrepresent. T1 cross-checks: company registry lookup, audit-firm registration check, ISO 27001 issuing-body lookup against IAF/national accreditation register. T3 escalations with vendors and cost bands: enhanced KYC/EDD (World-Check, Sayari), forensic accounting / quality-of-earnings, optional pen-test / SOC 2 review. Risk register covering identity, financial, regulatory, technical risks. Must-tell residuals.

evals.name: user-supplied-dataset-for-board-pres
evals.prompt: I have to present quarterly market-share numbers to our board on Thursday. The numbers come from a CSV one of our analysts pulled together — partly from a paid Nielsen feed, partly from public regulator filings, and partly from a few competitor websites she scraped. Walk me through what I should check before I rely on this dataset, including any verifications that cost money and would be worth doing for a board-level number.
evals.expected_output: Three-tier scrutiny across the dataset's three sources, treated as separate inputs. T1 cross-checks of public regulator filings (the source-of-truth, free). T2 questions about the Nielsen feed (license terms, vintage, methodology). T2 critique of the scraped competitor data (incentive: competitors don't have one to lie to scrapers, but data quality is unreliable). T3 escalation: paid market-research validation or a third-party audit firm. Risk register including data-quality, methodology, and reputational risk for the board itself. Must-tell residuals at top.
